title: Read and Predict Code
summary: Learn how to read, predict, and debug code.

steps.title: Reading Unfamiliar Code
steps.markdownContent: Look for structure first: identify the variables, the `setup()` function, and the `loop()`. Trace execution step by step.

quickCheck.question: When a program doesn't do what you expect, what do engineers call that mistake?
quickCheck.explanation: Flaws or mistakes in code logic are famously known as software bugs!
quickCheck.warmupExplanation: Even master engineers write bugs! Finding and fixing bugs is called debugging.

quickCheck.question: What is the best way to debug a program that isn't working?
options: Test one small piece at a time and read error messages
quickCheck.explanation: Testing small sections and reading compiler error messages helps pinpoint bugs quickly!
quickCheck.warmupExplanation: Detectives look for clues one by one. Debugging means finding clues to fix the code.

steps.title: Spotting Errors
steps.markdownContent: A syntax error (missing `;`, wrong bracket) stops code from compiling. A logic error (a condition that is never true) compiles but behaves incorrectly.

steps.title: Scientific Engineering Method
steps.markdownContent: Read the code → Predict what it will do → Test it → Observe the results → Explain why it happened.

steps.title: Syntax Error Debugger
steps.markdownContent: Find and fix syntax errors in this code.

steps.title: Engineering Prediction
steps.markdownContent: Predict the LED state based on this code logic.

steps.title: Knowledge Check
steps.markdownContent: Test what you learned about code reading and debugging.

questions.question: What is a syntax error?
options: A typo or grammar mistake in the code
The code doing the wrong thing
questions.explanation: Syntax errors violate the rules of the programming language.

questions.question: What is a logic error?
options: Code that compiles but does the wrong thing
questions.explanation: Logic errors occur when the code is grammatically correct but logically flawed.

questions.question: What should you do before running unfamiliar code?
options: Read and trace it step by step
questions.explanation: Tracing code helps you predict behavior and find errors.
